[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-11.90): Good morning, private banking, Marcus Lim speaking. Hello, Ms Tan. Nice to hear from you. Are you somewhere comfortable to talk, or would you prefer that I call you back?
[seg_0002] Client (12.30-22.61): Hi Marcus, Elaine here. Now is fine. I'm at home, and I've got my portfolio summary open beside me. I still prefer calling rather than typing everything into a message.
[seg_0003] Advisor (23.00-32.01): Certainly, we can speak over the phone. Before we get into the details, could you provide your identification particulars for the usual verification?
[seg_0004] Client (32.41-39.39): My NRIC is S zero nine three nine double five eight T. My date of birth is the ninth of October nineteen eighty-seven.
[seg_0005] Advisor (39.79-49.42): Thank you. Give me a moment to bring up your record. How has the gardening been going? Last time you mentioned spending more time on the balcony.
[seg_0006] Client (49.82-58.08): Quite nicely, actually. I've been repotting the herbs in the mornings before it gets too hot. The mint is taking over, so I had to give it its own pot.
[seg_0007] Advisor (58.48-67.19): Sounds like you've been busy. My mother has the same problem with hers. All right, I have your record up now, and I'm ready to listen.
[seg_0008] Client (67.59-72.79): The holding I want to reduce is Orion Global Income Fund. I want to sell, not add to the holding.
[seg_0009] Advisor (73.19-95.55): For Orion Global Income Fund, rising market interest rates can push down the value of the bonds it holds, which can lower the fund's value. If the bond issuers run into credit problems or default, the fund's value and income can also fall. Do you understand how rising interest rates and problems with the bond issuers can affect the fund's value and income?
[seg_0010] Client (95.95-103.98): Yes, I understand. Rising rates can reduce the value of the bonds, and issuer defaults can reduce the fund's value and the income it pays.
[seg_0011] Advisor (104.38-124.73): You could lose some or even all of the capital invested in this fund. Selling below what you originally paid would crystallise a loss. I recommend reducing your holding in Orion Global Income Fund because that reduces your exposure to interest-rate movements and issuer credit problems, making those factors less dominant in your portfolio.
[seg_0012] Client (125.13-140.80): Just a moment, please. The summary is open, but I've scrolled past the part I was looking at. The sale amount should be, let me find the entry on my summary— Ah, found the entry. The amount I want to sell is 75,000. The quantity for the sale is 500 units.
[seg_0013] Advisor (141.20-150.00): No problem, take your time with the screen. I'm still here. If the text is small, you can enlarge it without leaving this call.
[seg_0014] Client (150.40-169.53): It's okay, I can see it now. For this transaction, please use Singapore dollars as the settlement currency. Please place a limit order with a limit price of 150 Singapore dollars. Separately, my account in euros isn't showing on this portfolio screen. Could you check the display later? That account has nothing to do with this sale.
[seg_0015] Advisor (169.94-179.40): I'll look into the display issue separately after our call. If I need more information about the screen, I'll contact you rather than have you search through it now.
[seg_0016] Client (179.80-189.12): Thanks, a phone call would be best. Sometimes I don't notice messages until the evening, especially when I'm outside with the plants. You can leave a callback message if I miss you.
[seg_0017] Advisor (189.53-210.51): Certainly. Let me bring the conversation back to the final readback. To confirm your final instruction: sell 500 units of Orion Global Income Fund, for an amount of 75,000 in Singapore dollars, using a limit order with a limit price of 150 Singapore dollars. Do you confirm that instruction?
[seg_0018] Client (210.91-215.59): Yes, I confirm that final instruction exactly as you have stated it. Please proceed.
[seg_0019] Advisor (216.00-226.95): Thank you, Ms Tan. I'll handle the paperwork and follow up on the separate screen query. That's everything I need for this call. Enjoy the rest of your morning.
[seg_0020] Client (227.35-235.36): Thanks, Marcus. I'll put the laptop away and get back to my herbs before the sun reaches the balcony. Appreciate your time. Bye.

MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE  18 
5 PRICING CONTROLS AND DISCLOSURES 
 
5.1 PBs should establish requirements for RMs to provide clients with adequate 
pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should 
communicate to clients, and agree with them,  the fees1 charged to them in a timely and 
transparent way. Any d eviations from agreed pricing arrangements should be clearly 
disclosed to clients on a timely basis, with their agreement or “no objection”  properly 
documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.  
 
5.2 Fee schedules – All PBs provide clients with standard fee schedules at the time of 
account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

the sales of riskier products to these clients. Instances were also noted where clients were 
told by their RMs that the risk profiling exercise was a paper exercise. These observations 
reflect RMs’ lack of risk consciousness and adopting a perfunctory approach towards the 
risk profiling exercise. MAS expects PBs to inculcate the right mindset and understanding 
amongst front office staff with regard to clients’ safeguards and their duty to act in the 
interest of their clients. PBs should pay  attention to changes in clien ts’ profiles and 
implement controls to mitigate the risk of clients being unduly influenced to take on 
higher risk profiles or invest in products beyond their intended risk appetites. Examples of 
such controls include regular analyses of migration of clients’ profiles to identify unusual 
trends and patterns, and perform ance of independent sampling checks (e.g. listening to 
voice logs) to assess whether RMs inappropriately influenced clients to adopt a higher risk 
tolerance.

Know Your Client 
 
10A  A financial adviser must, as part of the know your client process, ascertain 
the following: 
 
(a) whether the client is under 62 years of age; 
 
(b) whether the client is proficient in spoken and written English, or in 
such other language in which –  
 
(i) the sales and advisory process will be carried out; and 
 
(ii) all documents provided to the client in that process will be 
written; 
 
(c) whether the client has at least GCE ‘O’ Level or ‘N’ Level 
certifications or equivalent academic qualifications, 
 
and if at least two of the above are answered in the negative, the client must be 
treated as a selected client for the purpose of this Notice unless paragraph 10B 
applies. 
[FAA-N16 (Amendment) 2025] 
 
10B  A financial adviser may choose not to treat a client mentioned in 
paragraph 10A as a selected client if  the financial adviser has reasons to 
conclude that the client possesses adequate knowledge and experience in any

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
